::: {.why}
You now have real fills and far too few of them, which makes this the right day to be precise about what a small sample can support rather than to fit a model anyway.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Estimate the impact coefficient from your own fills with an honest confidence interval.
- State what sample size you would need for the estimate to be useful, and what you will do until then.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>65 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Fit what you can: regress measured slippage on participation with the volatility scaling, using your own fills, and report the coefficient with its interval. The interval will be wide enough to include zero and also to include twice the published value, which is the correct conclusion from forty observations.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Compute the requirement: given the residual variance you observe, how many fills would you need for a 20 percent relative standard error on the coefficient? Then state the interim policy, which is to use the coefficient fitted to the ITCH sample in week 42 and to report your own estimate alongside it as it accumulates.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Set up the accumulation: a standing job that appends every new fill to the estimation dataset, so that by the capstone you have a real number rather than a plan to get one.
:::
:::

An impact coefficient from your own fills with an interval, the required sample size computed, and a standing accumulation job.
:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
Your own impact estimate has an interval spanning zero to twice the published value. What do you use, and what do you report?
:::
